patient._comment: 'patient' contains the three sections that may be exposed in the detailed patient display: presentation, answer, and clinical.

presentation._comment: The immutable patient evidence package available for triage. Panel context controls whether other sections are locked or available.
presentation.quote: My nose started bleeding an hour ago and I can't get it to quit. I've been pinching it. It's the front of my nose, dripping out the front — not down my throat.
presentation.triageNote: 60-year-old male with one hour of bleeding from the front of his nose. It slows with sustained pressure and is not running down his throat. He is not taking anticoagulants and remains hemodynamically stable.

answer._comment: The authoritative game answer. Explicit ESI, destination, and destination rationale are answer-bearing content; the player's assignment remains session state.
answer.destinationReason: ESI 5 is appropriate because this stable anterior nosebleed slows with pressure and is not expected to require a counted emergency resource.

clinical._comment: Display-ready clinical interpretation derived from patient.presentation. It preserves clinical meaning but must not explicitly name or identify the correct ESI level or destination; it does not participate in scoring.
clinical.summary: This patient has a likely anterior nasal bleed without anticoagulation, posterior flow, or hemodynamic compromise.
clinical.acuityReason: The bleeding responds to sustained compression and is not running down the throat, supporting simple local management.
keyFindings: One hour of anterior nasal bleeding
No blood running down the throat
teachingPoints: Firm uninterrupted pressure should be applied to the soft nasal alae while leaning forward.
Posterior bleeding, anticoagulation, airway difficulty, syncope, or instability would require escalation.

possibleClinicalOutcome.disposition: Compression and topical local treatment would likely control the bleeding, allowing discharge with prevention and recurrence instructions.

aiImageGeneration._comment: 'aiImageGeneration' is info for AI to generate the image of the patient. Most images were done with openAI gpt-image-1 using an API, not the app, in July 2026. Look for some python scripts that are used to create these images. Be sure that the anchor-image is available and is provided to the AI - otherwise the images will not be consistent.
aiImageGeneration.pose: seated, pinching the bridge of his nose with a tissue
signs: pinching his nose with a tissue
aiImageGeneration.prompt: Softly-shaded painterly cartoon illustration in a semi-realistic Pixar/Disney style: smooth gradient shading, soft natural lighting, gentle rounded volumes, fine delicate outlines (NOT thick flat cartoon outlines), warm detailed rendering, natural realistic proportions, single character, 3/4 front view, centered, square 1:1. Match the exact painterly style, brushwork, shading, line weight, lighting, and palette of the attached reference image. Subject: a white 60-year-old man, seated on a blue padded clinic chair. Pose: pinching the bridge of his nose with a tissue, head slightly forward. Expression: annoyed but calm. Clearly visible: pinching the nose with a bloodied tissue. No text, no logos.
